title: Exact mean age leaves a 20.23 umol/kg oxygen-use gap in a 2021 dual-tracer test with a fixed saturating law
abstract: We tested whether exact mean water age resolves oxygen ambiguity in a fixed oxygen-use model. We maximized the AOU difference between nonnegative age distributions that share tracer values. We used northern hemisphere atmospheric histories, a 90 umol/kg use scale, three age limits and three oxygen-use decay times. For 2021.5, ages from zero to 100 years and a 10-year use decay time, two distributions share exact CFC-12, SF6 and mean age of 15.67 years but differ in AOU by 20.23 umol/kg. A continuous-age certificate limits this gap to at most 20.235 on a fine grid. Exact CFC-11 lowers the worst-case gap to 11.44; an idealized argon-39 measurement leaves 20.22. A constant-source decay tracer matched to the oxygen-use function removes the gap in the exact case and limits it to 0.90 umol/kg with 0.5% source-normalized error. The code gives sharp grid bounds, positive witnesses and continuous-age error limits for 486 settings. These are global worst-case information limits with constructed mixtures. They are not field uncertainty estimates or a causal attribution of the California low. Source assumptions, the age-only oxygen law and free spectra limit the result.

display.caption: Worst-case AOU gaps for different measurements, oxygen-use times and error limits. All gaps are model information limits, not field estimates.
Constructed distributions share CFC-12, SF6 and mean age but differ in oxygen use under the same law.
